The Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social (IMSS) will extend specialty medical care to night shifts and weekends in Nuevo Laredo, part of a national plan to reduce appointment backlogs and avoid canceled procedures at the end of the year, according to Central de Noticias Tamaulipas.

The expanded hours build on the care already offered at local family medicine units, such as UMF No. 78, and will extend availability to hospital-level specialties starting Nov. 15.

IMSS Director General Zoé Robledo presented the plan during the morning news conference at the National Palace as part of the institutional program "12 acciones en 120 días," according to the report.

A digital appointment platform will begin operating Dec. 1 to keep the specialty appointment schedule running through December, a month when consultation availability has historically dropped.

The institute also announced extraordinary weekend surgery sessions in 20 medical units across the country, completing 561 surgeries in the first stage, and opened a call for 2,500 medical specialists, with recruitment sessions Nov. 18 and 19.

Specific dates and logistics for Nuevo Laredo patients will be announced in the coming days, according to the report.

Sources: Central de Noticias Tamaulipas.
